front: Which costs are included in inventory, and which are expensed?
back:
Included: purchase price, import duties, non-recoverable taxes, freight-in (less trade discounts), and conversion costs including allocated production overhead.
Expensed: abnormal waste, storage (unless necessary in production), administrative and selling costs.
Beginning inventory + Purchases - Ending inventory = COGS.

front: What are the inventory cost-flow methods and which are allowed under IFRS?
back: Specific identification, FIFO, weighted average cost and LIFO. LIFO is prohibited under IFRS; all four are allowed under U.S. GAAP.

front: FIFO vs LIFO when prices are rising
back:
FIFO: lowest COGS, highest income, highest inventory (near-current cost on the balance sheet).
LIFO: highest COGS, lowest income and taxes, lowest inventory (old layers on the balance sheet).

Perpetual updates inventory and COGS with every transaction; periodic computes COGS at period end from a count. FIFO (and specific identification) give the same result under both; LIFO and weighted average can differ.
LIFO reserve = FIFO inventory - LIFO inventory. It is disclosed by U.S. GAAP LIFO users so analysts can convert to FIFO.

front: How do you convert LIFO figures to FIFO?
back:
FIFO inventory = LIFO inventory + LIFO reserve.
FIFO COGS = LIFO COGS - change in LIFO reserve.
Equity adjustment = LIFO reserve x (1 - tax rate).
Selling more units than purchased so that old, low-cost LIFO layers flow into COGS. COGS falls below current cost and profit is temporarily inflated; analysts adjust for it.
Estimated selling price less estimated costs of completion and sale. Inventory is carried at the lower of cost and NRV.

front: IFRS vs U.S. GAAP on inventory write-down reversals
back: IFRS allows reversal if NRV recovers, limited to the original write-down (never above original cost). U.S. GAAP prohibits reversals.

front: Inventory turnover and days of inventory on hand
back:
Inventory turnover = COGS / average inventory.
Days of inventory on hand = 365 / inventory turnover. Compare companies only after putting them on the same cost-flow basis.

front: U.S. GAAP 'market' for LIFO and retail method inventory
back: Market is the middle value of replacement cost, NRV (ceiling) and NRV less normal profit margin (floor). Carry at the lower of cost and market.
